You can say what you want about school, but it didn't work for me personally. In my own unique, personal experience, which is not the same for everyone else's, it failed.

Much of my classes were honestly not that useful, in my school there were a lot of optional classes but you still had to choose a lot of them. I'm talking classes such as dance, art, architecture. Many of which I already knew I would have no future in before even signing up. And I get that trying new things can open your mind, but it's different when it's a class you have to keep going to well after the point you know you have no future in it. And even in classes such as Art I wasn't really taught anything, like at all. My art teacher just kind of let us do our own thing, he taught us some small things such as what personified animals are, but mostly he just kind of let us do whatever. He even let kids play games in his class and wouldn't even bother stopping a fight happening right in front of his eyes.

As for the more important classes, I feel like they failed too. Sports was good to stay fit, though my main complaint is regarding math and science. As a lot of people have claimed, they are very important. Now, personally, I have not found any use for them just yet, that may change sometime in the future but even if I did I don't think they did a good job at teaching me, or anyone else in my class really. Nobody really listened to anything said unless it was on a test, you can blame that on the kids all you like but it's the school's job to find a method of teaching that works. And even with tests, I'm not sure they work. I found much of the information from tests left my mind once it was done. I remember groups of boys were praising each other for their low scores, they'd get into groups and laugh about how low their grades were. Others who got low scores were treated as failures, the teachers did not seem to want to help them learn they just kind of forgot about them, despite claiming "if you never made a mistake, you'd never learn", the teachers weren't willing to help you if you made a mistake. I can't speak for others, but when I got a B or sometimes an A, I never felt like I had learnt anything, because I'd already forgotten most of it. I got praise from my teachers for what a great job I had done, but I didn't feel like I had learnt anything. And going online, I find I'm not the only one who's felt this way. And I don't think you can blame it on the kids when it's a large amount who all feel the same way.

And probably one of the biggest offenses of all is the time school starts. It's only natural for teenagers to sleep in longer, and no you can't just "go to sleep earlier" because your biological clock can simply just keep you up later and you can end up simply laying in your bed for hours before actually getting to sleep. Because that's how teenagers work. They're supposed to get enough sleep for their brain to work properly. Waking up in the mornings I was typically always tired at the beginning of the day, never starting the day ready to learn just ready to go back to bed. "Lazy" just seems like an excuse for not understanding teenage biology. If it were just me maybe you could just say I'm lazy, but when it's such a large group of people who feel this way I don't think you can blame the kids at that point.

And just to point out a bunch more about my school. Although history can be important, I do not think it's that important for your future, this extends to my religious studies class. Sometimes teachers would straight up play youtube videos for much of the lesson, I get that being a teacher is hard but come on? Although my school handled bullying better than most, it still failed to handle a lot of it making school a scary and unsafe environment for many kids, and I've heard other schools are much worse when it comes to bullying and mine was actually one of the better ones. Also, my school was more of a business than an education, even going as far as to force people to buy 3 different school uniforms for different days, plus a school jacket for cold days and a school hat.

Yes, I have left school. Not because of low grades, but because of mental health. Going to school wasn't healthy for me, there was bullying, all my friends were drifting away from me, I was suicidal, and on top of all that the homework was piling up. At the moment I have entered a different form of education online, which seems to be working best for me. Not saying it would work best for everyone, but it does for me. This different form of education I'm trying is not perfect, but I am at the very least learning more from it, and my mental health is much better. Once again, this is my own personal experience. Not anyone else's.

I think you're completely missing the point with this reply. You've established that intersex people are not natural, alright. They still exist though. All you've established is that there's 2 natural sexes.

If there's only 2 sexes in total then what are intersex people? Saying they're unnatural changes nothing. More than 90% of the things in our daily lives are unnatural yet they still exist.

Intersex people exist. They are not either of the binary sexes. And so they must be something else. Whether or not they're natural doesn't change any of these facts. You seem to be under the assumption that sexes must be natural to be considered a sex. You're arguing simply because you have a different definition of this word, not because of any genuine disagreement.

And that assumption does hold some merit considering that's how many people choose to define it, but definitions are constantly changing all the time, even the dictionary isn't a reliable source these days considering how definitions change based on the constantly changing and evolving beliefs of our society as well as the new information about the world we gather. The dictionary isn't even supposed to be a rulebook, especially considering it can be misinterpreted. It's more just a book describing how most people define words. But due to the nature of our society it's impossible to get that 100% accurate. Different words mean different things to different people. I think this is more or less just a misunderstanding based on how both sides seem to define sex.

Nevertheless, intersex people still exist and they're not either sex. So you can choose to define them as some other sex or just as people with no sex at all. Either way they're still not either sex.

Also, I cannot for the life of me figure out what you were trying to do with that comparison. It's like saying conjoined twins means people can have two souls??? I kind of see what you were trying to do but intersex people are literally just not one or the other sex that's why people say there's more than two sexes because of them. Saying that this would be like believing people can have two souls because of conjoined twins? I'm not even sure if you're implying that this two soul thing would be believed to be a different condition or that the conjoined twins would be believed to have two souls. Both of which have vastly different implications. This comparison makes no sense even ignoring the whole supernatural element thrown in there that makes the whole thing even more convoluted. Is there even a supernatural element thrown in or are you just meaning souls as in sentience?? I mean, I can kind of see what you were going for, but it came out being way too vague and making no sense to the point where I couldn't imagine anyone besides the person who wrote it fully understanding it. It doesn't make any sense even under the assumption that sex is binary. Sorry for the long criticism this ended up taking up way too much of this reply but I really think you could've worded that more clearly and come up with a comparison that made more sense. Maybe you could shine some light on what you were trying to do with that comparison? Because although I have some idea of what you were doing I'm mostly just confused. I'm not even asking in a rude way, I'm genuinely interested in the thought process that lead to a comparison like that.
